sources_considered.why: Human-versus-GPT-4 and GPT-4V comparison on ConceptARC from November 2023. It tests abstraction and flexible generalisation, plus some visual grid comprehension.
GPT-4 technical report. It claims human-level results on many language-heavy benchmarks, which is relevant to the semantics part.
Its benchmark table (WinoGrande 87.5%, HellaSwag 95.3%) is relevant, but the text extracts as broken table lines with no clean quotable sentence. Mentioned only in the gaps.

receipt.public_excerpt: However, GPT-4’s performance remains well below the high performance of humans, supporting the conclusion that, even with more informative prompting, the system lacks basic abstract reasoning abilities tested by this corpus.

evidence_items.explanation: In November 2023, GPT-4 solved 33% of ConceptARC tasks against about 91% for humans. This supports the 'cognitively flexible' part. It says nothing on its own about world models, 3D navigation, or language semantics.

receipt.public_excerpt: The visual one-shot prompt resulted in an accuracy of 0.23 over the 48 minimal tasks, compared with 0.69 for the (temperature 0) text-only counterpart.

evidence_items.explanation: GPT-4V did poorly on simple visual grid tasks that humans solve about 95% of the time. This bears loosely on visual comprehension, but abstract grids are not natural scenes.

receipt.public_excerpt: While less capable than humans in many real-world scenarios, GPT-4 exhibits human-level performance on various professional and academic benchmarks, including passing a simulated bar exam with a score around the top 10% of test takers.

evidence_items.explanation: OpenAI reports human-level scores on many language-heavy exams. This cuts against a plain reading that AI was 'pretty poor' at getting meaning from language. Whether exam scores measure semantic understanding is itself disputed.

unresolved_gaps: No 2023 human-versus-AI evaluation was found for 'maintaining cognitive models of the world', 'navigating 3D world', or natural-scene comprehension.

On language semantics, GPT-4's reported benchmark scores (for example WinoGrande 87.5% in the technical report table) are close to human level. Whether that counts as 'pretty poor' depends on a reading the speaker did not supply.
